title: Misinformation Regarding Medical and Social Effects of HPV Vaccination
what_it_is: Misinformation Regarding Medical and Social Effects of HPV Vaccination

sections.label: School HPV vaccination programme
sections.summary: The Health Promotion Board rolled out a national school-based HPV vaccination programme for Secondary 1 female students on 1 April, covering 25 schools by 26 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) rolled-out the national school-based human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme for Secondary 1 female students on 1 April this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As of 26 April 2019, 25 schools have been covered by the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Ninety-three percent of the students in these schools have opted for the vaccine.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: HPV vaccination has been shown to be safe and effective and is recommended by the World Health Organization and leading health agencies for the prevention of cervical cancer, a serious disease and one of the top 10 cancers among women in Singapore.

sections.label: Reasons parents decline vaccination
sections.summary: Most parents declining said their daughters already had the HPV vaccination or preferred primary care clinics, with under 1% concerned about safety and side effects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As regards the reasons, most of them either say that their daughters had already taken the HPV vaccination or that they prefer to bring them to the primary care clinics themselves for the vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have a small percentage of less than 1% of parents who actually are concerned with the safety and side effects of the vaccine.

sections.label: No evidence of earlier sex
sections.summary: A scan of studies and evidence elsewhere shows no evidence that HPV-vaccinated females have sex earlier or have more partners than unvaccinated females.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to the third question on social effects of HPV vaccination, our scan of studies as well as evidence elsewhere shows that there is no evidence that those females who have got HPV vaccine or are vaccinated will have sex earlier or will have more partners than unvaccinated females.
